{"author": null, "closed_at": null, "collaborating_teams": null, "collaborating_users": null, "created_at": null, "credits": [], "credits_detailed": [], "cve_id": null, "cvss": {"score": null, "vector_string": null}, "cvss_severities": {"cvss_v3": {"score": null, "vector_string": null}, "cvss_v4": {"score": 6.3, "vector_string": "CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N"}}, "cwe_ids": ["CWE-502"], "cwes": [{"cwe_id": "CWE-502", "name": "Deserialization of Untrusted Data"}], "description": "# Advisory 19 — [H16] Relay HMAC unmarshalToken runs gob.Decoder on unauth bytes before signature check

- **Severity:** Medium (reassessed by NetBird; see Impact)
- **CVSS 4.0 Base Score:** **6.3** (reassessed by NetBird)
- **CVSS 4.0 Vector:** `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- **CWE:** [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html) (CWE-502)
- **Affected product:** `github.com/netbirdio/netbird` — relay server, `>= 0.29.0, < 0.75.0` (reported against v0.74.3)
- **Affected component(s):** relay server pre-authentication handshake
- **Reporter:** [@SecurinDisclose](https://github.com/SecurinDisclose) — Arjun Basnet · Securin Inc. — `arjun.basnet@securin.io`

---

## Overview

```go
func unmarshalToken(raw []byte) (*Token, error) {
    var t Token
    if err := gob.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw)).Decode(&t); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return &t, nil
}
```

The relay accepts attacker-supplied bytes and hands them to `gob.NewDecoder`
before any HMAC signature verification. Any future gob decoder CVE (or existing
resource-exhaustion primitive) is directly reachable pre-auth by an anonymous
network client.

The reachable path is the deprecated `Hello` handshake. `handshakeReceive`
dispatched a `MsgTypeHello` message to `handleHelloMsg`, which called the
validator's `ValidateHelloMsgType` — the gob path — before any peer was
authenticated. The `Auth` handshake that every client has used since v0.29.1
never invoked gob.

---

## Affected Location

Paths and line numbers as of v0.74.7, the last affected release:

- `shared/relay/auth/hmac/token.go:21` — `unmarshalToken` uses `gob.Decoder`.
- `shared/relay/auth/hmac/validator.go:22-33` — signature check runs AFTER decode.
- `shared/relay/auth/validator.go` — `ValidateHelloMsgType` delegates to the above.
- `relay/server/handshake.go` — `handshakeReceive` accepts `MsgTypeHello` pre-authentication and routes it to `handleHelloMsg`.

---

## Vulnerable Code

```go
func unmarshalToken(raw []byte) (*Token, error) {
    var t Token
    if err := gob.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw)).Decode(&t); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return &t, nil
}
```

```go
func (a *TimedHMACValidator) Validate(credentials any) error {
    b, ok := credentials.([]byte)
    if !ok {
        return fmt.Errorf("invalid credentials type")
    }
    c, err := unmarshalToken(b)                 // gob decode of unauthenticated bytes
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    return a.TimedHMAC.Validate(sha256.New, c)  // signature verified afterwards
}
```

---

## Reproduction

Sending a `Hello` handshake message to a relay server older than v0.75.0 reaches
the gob decoder without credentials.

### PoC output

```
=== RUN   TestH16_GobDecoderSurface
    poc_test.go:37: crafted payload 128MB nested slices -> peak alloc 1.9GB
    poc_test.go:42: server accepted decode before signature check
--- PASS: TestH16_GobDecoderSurface
```

The reported allocation figure comes from calling `unmarshalToken` directly. Over
the wire the payload is bounded — see Impact.

---

## Impact

Reaching the decoder needs no credentials, but the achievable input is small.
`handshakeReceive` reads into a buffer of `messages.MaxHandshakeSize` (212
bytes), and the pre-authentication phase is bounded by a 10-second timeout, so at
most a couple of hundred attacker-controlled bytes ever reach `gob.Decode`. The
128 MB payload in the PoC is not reachable through the server, and there is no
confidentiality or integrity impact.

What the path did expose is `encoding/gob` itself, which has had denial-of-service
vulnerabilities — for example CVE-2024-34156, stack exhaustion on deeply nested
input, fixed in Go 1.22.7 and 1.23.1. A relay server built with an affected Go
toolchain would have reached that from an unauthenticated connection, before any
signature check.

NetBird therefore rates this Medium (CVSS 4.0 base score 6.3) rather than the
reported High (7.7). The difference is in the availability metrics: the report
assumes a high availability impact on the relay and on subsequent systems, which
the 212-byte handshake bound does not support. What remains is a low availability
impact, contingent on a separate decoder vulnerability and so marked as attack
requirements present. It stays network-reachable and pre-authentication, which is
why it does not fall lower. CIA breakdown is captured in the reassessed CVSS 4.0
vector: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`.

---

## Fix

Fixed in v0.75.0 ([#6783](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/6783)). The
relay server no longer accepts the `Hello` message type, and the gob-based token
and message decoding behind it was deleted along with the legacy validator
wiring. Handshake authentication now runs only through the `Auth` message, whose
token is parsed by `v2.UnmarshalToken` — a fixed-layout byte reader with explicit
length checks — and whose signature is verified against the declared algorithm's
digest size. No gob decoding remains on the relay server's handshake path.

The `Hello` handshake shipped in v0.29.0 and was superseded by the `Auth`
handshake in v0.29.1. From v0.29.1 onward no NetBird client used it; the server
kept the path solely for backwards compatibility with pre-v0.29.1 clients, which
is why it could be removed outright rather than reordered.

Operators running a relay server older than v0.75.0 should upgrade. No
configuration change is required, and no client action is needed.

---

## Remediation

1. HMAC-verify the raw bytes before ever calling `gob.Decode`.
2. Prefer a length-bounded, schema-driven format (protobuf) over gob for network payloads.
3. Cap decoder input size and nesting depth defensively.

---

## References & Evidence

- **CWE definitions:** [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)
- **CVSS 4.0 calculator:** https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/4-0
- **Fix:** [#6783](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/6783)

---

## Credit

Reported by **Arjun Basnet** — [Securin Inc.](https://securin.io) — via GitHub [@SecurinDisclose](https://github.com/SecurinDisclose).
Coordinated disclosure timeline: **90 days** — public disclosure on or after **2026-10-11** unless extended by mutual agreement.

---

**https://github.com/SecurinDisclose/netbird-0.74.3-audit** (private — request read access via GitHub or email `arjun.basnet@securin.io`).
